candidates.name: Hidradenocarcinoma
support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement. Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm.
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
candidates.why: The histopathological features and immunohistochemical profile are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a rare malignant tumor of apocrine gland origin.

candidates.name: Apocrine carcinoma
support_spans: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
candidates.why: The presence of apocrine glands and the expression of GATA3 and estrogen receptor suggest a possible diagnosis of apocrine carcinoma.

candidates.name: Extramammary Paget disease
support_spans: erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Positive for: cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15
candidates.why: The clinical presentation and immunohistochemical profile are consistent with extramammary Paget disease, a rare skin malignancy.

candidates.name: Cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer
support_spans: Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
contradict_spans: Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors
candidates.why: The immunohistochemical profile and the presence of tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node are concerning for a cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer, although imaging studies did not reveal a primary breast tumor.

unexplained_specific_evidence: Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

selector.rationale: Hidradenocarcinoma is supported by the dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, Indian file pattern of tumor cells, and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.

rejected.label: Apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: Although apocrine glands are present, the primary evidence points towards a more specific diagnosis of Hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer
rejected.why: Imaging studies revealed no evidence of primary or secondary breast tumors, contradicting this diagnosis.
